title: Pick the right tool from a pile and hand it over handle first
instruction: I'm setting concrete pavers and need to tap them down without chipping them. Find the tool for that in the pile and hand it to me handle first: lay its handle across my open palm with the head out past my thumb, pointing away from me, then let go. Leave the other tools on the bench.
context: The core of this task is choosing the tool from the job and getting it out of a pile; a safe, one-handed, handle-first handover is the finish. The instruction names the job, not the tool: tapping concrete pavers down without chipping them calls for a rubber mallet, since a steel hammer chips them (Angi, "Tools and Materials Needed to Install Concrete Pavers"; EngineerFix, "Why You Need a Rubber Mallet for Pavers"; Angi, "How to Lay Pavers": tap high spots down with a rubber mallet). The pile holds a look-alike steel cross-peen hammer, and the mallet lies under two other tools that must be lifted off it first. Paving is a trade of its own (O*NET 47-4091.00, Segmental Pavers). Handing a tool handle first, head away from the person, lets them take it by the grip.
setup: Station table, fixed layout (object_jitter=0); cm, x away from the robot, y to its left. In the middle, four NVIDIA SimReady hand tools in a heap: a rubber mallet (39.4 cm, 585 g, black rubber head 7.1 cm across, orange and black handle) lies on its side at x 30, handle along y (head y 9 to 16.5, handle end y -23); a steel fork pry bar with a square back end (20.7 cm, 131 g) and a Phillips No. 1 screwdriver (14.7 cm, 49 g; steel shaft, black and orange grip) lie across its handle at y 7 and y -11.7, one end each on the table; a cross-peen hammer (39.4 cm, 1.35 kg, dark steel head, orange handle) lies flat beside it at x 47, head to the right (y -22 to -14). On the left, a coworker's hand in a hi-vis yellow glove (fixed boxes) lies palm up on the table: palm x 31 to 41, y 35.5 to 44.5, 4 cm high; four fingers 2 cm wide, 6.6 to 8.8 cm long and 1.8 cm thick, toward the robot; on its left a thumb web (6 x 2.2 cm, 0.5 cm high) and the thumb lying flat (10 x 3.2 cm), its top 2.2 cm below the palm's; a glove cuff (4 x 7 x 3.6 cm high) and a navy sleeve (46 x 8 x 6.5 cm high) run to the table's far edge, where the coworker stands (body at x 108, y 20).
scoring: Scored at the end; a full score must hold for 1 s. 0 if the arms' state can't be read. 0 if, at any point, the mallet was dropped (once no gripper holds it, its outline centre falls 2 cm below where a gripper last held it, or it moves down faster than 0.63 m/s, the speed of a 2 cm free fall) or dragged out of the pile (its outline centre 2 cm or more from where it lay, in plan, while a cover within 5 cm of where it lay still overlaps its outline in plan and in height), or another tool was knocked about (moving over 5 cm/s with no gripper's tool point within 5 cm of it, 2 control steps in a row, after the first second); or if, at the end, any tool has fallen (its outline's centre off the table or 5 cm below its top), the hammer's outline centre is more than 5 cm from where it lay, or another tool is up (its outline's middle 7 cm or more above the table), held by a gripper, or lies on the coworker (its outline over the hand, cuff or sleeve and within 3 cm above it). A gripper holds a tool when its tool point is within 3 cm of the tool's outline, its fingers are closed to under 8.5 cm, and the line between its pads crosses the outline. Otherwise: 1.0 if handed over properly, every gripper within 10 cm of the mallet open at least 6 cm with its tool point at least 3 cm from the mallet's outline, and all tools still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), held for 1 s (20 steps); 0.75 if handed over properly: the handle lies across the palm (its underside over the palm's centre -4 to +8 mm from the palm's top), its head pointing toward the thumb, away from the coworker's body, within 25 degrees, the handle within 10 degrees of level, and the point of the handle over the palm's centre 1 to 7 cm from where the handle meets the head; 0.5 if the handle rests on the palm any other way; 0.25 with its head on the palm (head first), or if a gripper holds it up (7 cm or more) or within 7 cm of the palm's centre. Caps: 0.25 if the head was aimed within 30 degrees of the coworker's body while carried with its outline within 15 cm of the palm's centre (2 steps in a row); 0.5 if any point of it moved faster than 0.25 m/s while carried with its outline within 15 cm of the palm's centre (2 steps), or a gripper's tool point or finger pads (not its wrist) came within 3 mm of the coworker. Holding, letting go and touching are judged from geometry.
reset_notes: Fixed layout. Each reset puts every tool back 1.5 mm above its resting pose and lets the heap settle for 0.5 s (the pry bar settles at about 17.2 degrees, the screwdriver at 16.7). The hand is fixed: nothing to clean up.
fidelity: Tools are NVIDIA SimReady scans (CC BY 4.0) at real size with the asset's own mass, friction and collision, loaded by a scene hook. The mallet's and hammer's centres of mass and principal moments are replaced by a head-plus-handle model (the assets' are wrong); every tool's spin is damped 2/s (PhysX has no rolling resistance). The hand is static boxes and can't close: the mallet must rest on the open palm. No finger contact sensing: holding, letting go and touching are judged from geometry.
